newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Two survivors found in Malaysia helicopter crash.
newsitem.headline: Two survivors found in Malaysia helicopter crash.

text.p: Rescuers found two survivors and two bodies but were still looking for another three crew members after a Malaysian air force helicopter crashed into the sea, the national Bernama news agency said on Thursday.

The helicopter, with seven people on board, went down in bad weather on Wednesday, 44 miles off Teluk Bahang on Malaysia's northern Penang island. It had been on a mission to airlift an injured Thai sailor from a Thai-registered ship, Jupiter II.
Pilot Daud Sulaiman and crew member Bentara Kanan Hakimi were rescued early on Thursday after suffering minor injuries. The team of more than 70 rescuers later found the two bodies.
Three other crew on the U.S.-made Sikorsky S-61 were still missing, rescue officials said.

The Thai sailor, Somsak Mant, said the helicopter crashed while one of the crew members was being winched down to the Jupiter II. Somsak said he had been scalded while trying to repair the ship, which had stalled in seas southwest of Penang.

Bernama said the crash was the ninth involving a Malaysian airforce aircraft this year. It said some 60 people had died in crashes involving the Sikorsky since the helicopter was introduced in Malaysia 28 years ago.
